question_text: What is the genotype of the wrinkled phenotype of pea seeds?

insider_note: The answer is two letters, so the second mark has to come from the REASON. Say that a recessive character needs both alleles recessive.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Principles of Inheritance and Variation (Botany-II) · 2 marks

steps.label: The genotype
steps.margin_note: Two letters plus which allele is dominant. Three lines.
lines: The genotype of the wrinkled phenotype is rr —
steps.why: Wrinkled is the recessive character in Mendel's seed-shape pair, so it can only show in the homozygous recessive genotype.
common_mistakes: Writing Rr. Rr would be ROUND, because R is dominant.
Writing RR. RR is round as well.
steps.memory_tip: Wrinkled is recessive, so it must be rr.

steps.label: Why it must be that
steps.margin_note: The rule, the three genotypes, and the useful consequence.

lines.text: A recessive character shows only when BOTH

lines: A recessive character is expressed only when NO
RR and Rr are both round; only rr is wrinkled.
So a wrinkled seed can have only ONE possible
genotype, and its genotype is known by sight.
steps.why: A recessive phenotype is the one case where appearance alone settles the genotype, which is exactly why a test cross uses a recessive parent.
common_mistakes: Saying a wrinkled seed could be Rr. It could not; Rr is round.
Giving no reason. The genotype alone is only half the answer.
steps.memory_tip: Recessive on the outside means recessive twice on the inside.
